C++ (founded 1983) is the earliest of the four.
MATLAB (founded 1984) is the earliest of the four.
Who among these is an astronomer?
Dorothea Klumpke is an astronomer. Dorothea Klumpke Roberts (August 9, 1861 in San Francisco – October 5, 1942 in San Francisco) was an American astronomer.
Which one below is best known as a mathematician?
Eric Weinstein is a mathematician. Eric Ross Weinstein (born October 26, 1965) is an American investor and podcast host.
What is the atomic number of Unbinilium?
Unbinilium, also known as eka-radium or element 120, is a hypothetical chemical element; it has symbol Ubn and atomic number 120.
What is the atomic number of Arsenic?
Arsenic is a chemical element; it has the symbol As and atomic number 33.
In what year did Ted Kaczynski die?
Ted Kaczynski: The FBI used the case identifier UNABOM (University and Airline Bombing) before his identity was known, resulting in the media naming him the "Unabomber".
In what year was Angelman syndrome discovered?
Angelman syndrome (AS) is a rare genetic disorder that affects approximately 1 in 15,000 individuals.

Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-19: Russian Aircraft Corporation MiG. The Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-19 (Russian: Микоян и Гуревич МиГ-19; NATO reporting name: Farmer) is a Soviet second generation, single-seat, twinjet fighter aircraft.
Yakovlev MC-21: United Aircraft Corporation. The aircraft made its maiden flight on 28 May 2017 from Irkutsk.
Who is credited with discovering Lynx?
Lynx (constellation): Johannes Hevelius. Lynx is a constellation named after the animal, usually observed in the Northern Celestial Hemisphere.
Who is credited with discovering Newton's law of universal gravitation?
Newton's law of universal gravitation: Robert Hooke. This is a general physical law derived from empirical observations by what Isaac Newton called inductive reasoning.
Who is credited with discovering Pulsar?
Pulsar: Jocelyn Bell Burnell. This produces a very precise interval between pulses that ranges from milliseconds to seconds for an individual pulsar.
Who is credited with discovering Coma Berenices?
Coma Berenices: Conon of Samos. Coma Berenices is an ancient asterism in the northern sky, which has been defined as one of the 88 modern constellations.
A "classic organochlorine" insecticide once heavily used to treat seed and soil, it was banned in most countries by the 1990s after proving a persistent, bioaccumulating pollutant. What is it?
Aldrin is an organochlorine insecticide that was widely used until the 1990s, when it was banned in most countries.
Named for the Portuguese word for indigo shrub, this simplest aromatic amine smells of rotten fish, ignites into a smoky flame, and is a key precursor to polyurethane and dyes — what compound is it?
Aniline (From) is an organic compound with the formula C6H5NH2.

Around 1920, when the energy source of stars was a complete mystery, which English astrophysicist boldly and correctly guessed it was the fusion of hydrogen into helium — and lent his name to a natural ceiling on a star's brightness?
Arthur Eddington (28 December 1882 - 22 November 1944) was an English astrophysicist and mathematician.

An Arctic and sub-Arctic cetacean, it is one of two living members of the family Monodontidae and is also known as the white whale (the only cetacean regularly occurring with this color) and the sea canary for its high-pitched calls. What is it?
Beluga whale (Delphinapterus leucas), is an Arctic and sub-Arctic cetacean.

This semi-solid tissue inside the spongy portions of bones serves as the primary site of new blood cell production in birds and mammals, making up roughly 5% of an adult human's body mass — what tissue is it?
Bone marrow is a semi-solid tissue found within the spongy (also known as cancellous) portions of bones.
Its three-dimensional shape mimics adenosine closely enough to plug into the same receptors, blocking the brain's signal to wind down — which psychoactive substance is it?
Caffeine is a central nervous system (CNS) stimulant of the methylxanthine class and is the most commonly consumed psychoactive substance globally.

A cultivated variety of the same species as cabbage and broccoli, this vegetable's edible part is a dense head of undeveloped flower buds called the curd — one variety, Romanesco, grows its curds in stunning fractal spirals. Name this vegetable?
Charted in 1756 by Lacaille and named for the drafting tool that draws circles, this faint southern constellation is easily confused with the mariner's-compass constellation Pyxis. Which one is it?
Circinus is a small, faint constellation in the southern sky, first defined in 1756 by the French astronomer Nicolas-Louis de Lacaille.
This inorganic compound's blue crystalline pentahydrate form was historically called blue vitriol, while its anhydrous form is white and dissolves in water to form an octahedral complex. What is it?
Copper(II) sulfate is an inorganic compound with the chemical formula CuSO4.
Born at the Point McLeay Mission in 1872, this preacher and inventor who registered 10 patents is widely credited as the first Aboriginal Australian published author — who is he?
David Unaipon was an Aboriginal Australian preacher, inventor, and writer who has been widely credited as the first Aboriginal published author.
Fossils of this Late Devonian armored fish genus, among the earliest vertebrate apex predators ever, have turned up from Morocco to Poland to North America — which genus?
Dunkleosteus is an extinct genus of large arthrodire ("jointed-neck") fish that existed during the Late Devonian period, about 382-358 million years ago.

Often used to keep blood pressure from dropping during anesthesia, this stimulant has also been tried against asthma, obesity, and even narcolepsy — though it's no longer the preferred fix. What is it?
Ephedrine is a central nervous system (CNS) stimulant and sympathomimetic agent that is often used to prevent low blood pressure during anesthesia.
This type of anaerobic metabolism harnesses the redox potential of reactants like glucose to produce ATP without needing oxygen. What process is it?
Fermentation is a type of anaerobic metabolism that harnesses the redox potential of the reactants to make adenosine triphosphate (ATP) and organic end products.

Lasting anywhere from milliseconds to hours, these are the most luminous explosions in the universe after the Big Bang, sometimes triggered when massive stars collapse into black holes — what are they?
Gamma-ray burst (GRBs) are extremely energetic events occurring in distant galaxies that represent the brightest and most powerful class of explosion in the Universe.

Dating back roughly 250 million years to the early Triassic, these ground-dwelling herbivorous insects use powerful hind legs to leap away from danger and hatch as nymphs that molt five times — what's the insect?
Grasshopper are a group of insects belonging to the suborder Caelifera.
This naturally occurring molecule and medication is a powerful blood anticoagulant used to treat heart attacks and prevent clotting in dialysis machines and test tubes — what is it?
Heparin (UFH), is a medication and naturally occurring glycosaminoglycan.
In organisms whose total cell count is fixed at maturity, this cell-enlargement process drives nearly all further growth after the embryonic stage — what is it?
Hypertrophy is an increase in the size of individual cells.

In 1897, this British physicist showed that cathode rays were made of previously unknown negatively charged particles far smaller than atoms — the first subatomic particle ever identified. Who was he?
J. J. Thomson (18 December 1856 - 30 August 1940) was a British physicist.
This 19th-century French mathematician ranged across number theory, complex analysis, and mathematical physics — and his name now sits on a crater on the Moon. Who was he?

Joseph Liouville (24 March 1809 - 8 September 1882) was a French mathematician who worked on a number of different fields in mathematics, including number theory, complex analysis, and mathematical physics.
This broadly distributed genus of spiders is informally grouped under a nickname referencing marital loss, encompassing both black and brown members — what is its scientific name?
Latrodectus is a broadly distributed genus of spiders informally called the widow spiders, with several species that are commonly known as the true widows.
Prized as one of the most profitable seafood commodities in the coastal waters where it's caught, this clawed crustacean spends its life in crevices and burrows on the sea floor - which creature?
Lobster are malacostracan decapod crustaceans of the family Nephropidae or its synonym Homaridae.
Its bell-shaped flowers give way to yellow or orange berries, but this nightshade genus is better known by the folkloric root that inspired countless myths and superstitions — which genus?
Mandragora (genus) is a plant genus belonging to the nightshade family (Solanaceae).
This scientific field studies Earth's atmosphere and short-term weather phenomena, with a central focus on forecasting — name the discipline?
Meteorology is the scientific study of the Earth's atmosphere and short-term atmospheric phenomena (i.e., weather), with a focus on weather forecasting.
These small, non-vascular, flowerless plants form dense green clumps or mats in damp, shady spots — name this group of plants?
Moss are small, non-vascular flowerless plants in the taxonomic division Bryophyta sensu stricto.
This form of vitamin B3 is taken orally to treat pellagra without the skin-flushing side effect of niacin, and used as a cream to fight acne and reduce signs of aging skin — what's the compound?
Nicotinamide (INN, BAN UK) or niacinamide (USAN US) (IUPAC name: 3-pyridinecarboxoamide) is a form of vitamin B3 found in food and used as a dietary supplement and medication.
This flowering herb in the mint family, native to the Mediterranean, is sometimes called wild marjoram and is a staple of countless savory dishes. What is it?
Oregano (Origanum vulgare) is a species of flowering plant in the mint family, Lamiaceae.
First domesticated in Neolithic China and rarely living past twenty years, this deciduous fruit tree also produces a smooth-skinned variety commercially sold as a different fruit — which tree?
Peach (Prunus persica) is a deciduous tree that bears edible juicy fruits with various characteristics.
Whether captured electronically on a sensor or chemically on light-sensitive film, this art and practice of recording light also powers science and manufacturing — think photolithography. What is it?

Photography is the art, application, and practice of creating images by recording light, either electronically by means of an image sensor, or chemically by means of a light-sensitive material such as photographic film.
This autonomic nervous system disorder causes an abnormally large jump in heart rate — thirty beats per minute within ten minutes — simply from sitting up or standing. What condition is it?
Postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome (POTS) is a condition characterized by an abnormally large increase in heart rate upon sitting up or standing.
One of America's top rocketry and high-speed-flight experts, this engineer helped found engineering cybernetics before being deported to China in 1955. Who was he?

Qian Xuesen (December 11, 1911 - October 31, 2009; also spelled as Tsien Hsue-shen) was a Chinese aerospace engineer and cyberneticist who made significant contributions to the field of aerodynamics and established engineering cybernetics.
With Patrick Steptoe and Jean Purdy, this British physiologist pioneered the technique that led to the 1978 birth of Louise Brown, earning a 2010 Nobel Prize. Who was he?
Robert Edwards (physiologist) (27 September 1925 - 10 April 2013) was a British physiologist and pioneer in reproductive medicine, and in-vitro fertilisation (IVF) in particular.
Spanning continents from North America to temperate Asia, this genus covers the majority of the world's common bushy-tailed squirrels — which genus?
Sciurus (or) contains most of the common, bushy-tailed squirrels in North America, Europe, temperate Asia, Central America and South America.
About 0.01% of people are born with this condition, in which the heart typically ends up on the right side of the chest instead of the left — what is it?
Situs inversus is a congenital condition in which the major visceral organs are reversed or mirrored from their normal positions.
Also known as sea stars, roughly 1,900 species of these star-shaped marine invertebrates live on seabeds from warm tropics to icy polar oceans. What are they?
Starfish are a class of marine invertebrates generally shaped like a star polygon.
A staple corm across African, Caribbean, Oceanian, and Asian cultures, this root vegetable of the arum family is often likened to yams — what is it?
Taro (Colocasia esculenta) is a root vegetable.

Sitting at the organizational level between individual cells and a full organ, this biological term for a functional grouping of similar cells derives from a French word meaning 'to weave' — what is it?
Tissue (biology) is an assembly of similar cells and their extracellular matrix from the same embryonic origin that together carry out a specific function.

An oily, amber-colored liquid that's extremely non-volatile and therefore lingers in the environment, this organophosphorus compound was developed for chemical warfare and is lethal in doses of just tens of milligrams — which chemical agent?
VX (nerve agent) is an extremely toxic synthetic chemical compound in the organophosphorus class, specifically, a thiophosphonate.

This American physical chemist built ultra-sensitive Geiger counters and once worked on the Manhattan Project — but his 1960 Nobel came for a dating method that revolutionized archaeology and paleontology. Who was he?

Willard Libby (December 17, 1908 - September 8, 1980) was an American physical chemist noted for his role in the 1949 development of radiocarbon dating, a process which revolutionized archaeology and palaeontology.
The first Muslim scientist to win a Nobel Prize, this Pakistani theoretical physicist shared the 1979 Physics prize for unifying the weak and electromagnetic forces — who was he?
First flown in October 1972, this was the world's first twin-engine wide-body airliner, born from a 1967 France-West Germany-UK collaboration that later lost its British partner — what is it?
Airbus A300: World's first twin-engine widebody jet airliner.
Sold under the brand name Xanax, this fast-acting benzodiazepine is most often prescribed for panic disorder and generalized anxiety — what drug is it?
Alprazolam: Benzodiazepine medication. Alprazolam is most commonly prescribed in the management of anxiety disorders, especially panic disorder and generalized anxiety disorder (GAD).
Likened to a bubble or balloon, this outward bulge forms at a weak spot in a blood-vessel wall and grows ever more dangerous as it risks rupture — what is it?
Aneurysm: Bulge in the wall of a blood vessel. An aneurysm is an outward bulging, likened to a bubble or balloon, caused by a localized, abnormal, weak spot on a blood vessel wall.
Also known as pirarucu or paiche, this native of the Amazon River basin is among the largest freshwater fish on Earth — what species is it?
The third-largest fish in its family, behind Siberian taimen and Pacific Chinook, this species is unusual for surviving spawning and returning to sea to breed again — which fish?
Atlantic salmon: Species of fish. The Atlantic salmon (Salmo salar) is a species of ray-finned fish in the family Salmonidae.
Bred in Britain to hunt rabbits and hares, this scent hound's keen nose also makes it a popular detection dog for smuggled food at airports — which breed?
Beagle: Breed of small scent hound. The Beagle is a British breed of scent hound, similar in appearance to the much larger foxhound.
Patented in 1976 and sold under the brand name Zebeta, this beta-1-selective medication treats high blood pressure and heart failure — what is it?
Bisoprolol: Beta-1 selective adrenenergic blocker medication used to treat cardiovascular diseases.
Hailing from the Anglo-Scottish frontier and frequently cited as the most intelligent dog breed on Earth, which sheepdog dominates sheepdog trials?
Border Collie: Working dog breed. The Border Collie is a breed of British herding dog of the collie type of medium size.
Encompassing reporting, dashboards, data mining, and analytics, this set of strategies and technologies helps companies turn raw data into strategic decisions — what's it called?
Business intelligence: Strategies for analysis and use of data.
Nicknamed for its heart-shaped seed pods, this mustard-family weed is considered protocarnivorous because its seeds ooze a mucilage that traps nematodes — which species?
Capsella bursa-pastoris: Species of flowering plant in the mustard family.

This biological process splits a parent into two daughters, either producing genetically identical copies via mitosis or reducing chromosome number by half via meiosis to form gametes. What process is it?
Cell division: Biological process. Cell division usually occurs as part of a larger cell cycle in which the cell grows and replicates its chromosome(s) before dividing.

This antibiotic is used as an eye ointment for conjunctivitis and, when safer options fail, to treat meningitis, plague, cholera, and typhoid — but in newborns it can trigger a dangerous swelling condition called gray baby syndrome — what drug is it?
Chloramphenicol: Antibiotic. Chloramphenicol is an antibiotic useful for the treatment of a number of bacterial infections.
This French inventor born near Toulouse is remembered chiefly as an aviation pioneer, but in 1870 he was also among the first to take up the sport of cycling in France — who is it?
Clément Ader: French inventor and engineer (1841–1925)

Native to Europe and North Africa, this member of the carrot family can grow to 8 feet tall, with hollow stems blotched dark maroon and a distinctly foul smell carried on the wind — which highly poisonous plant is this?
Conium maculatum: Poisonous plant. The plant is herbaceous, with no woody parts, and has a biennial lifecycle.
A creeping vine of the gourd family that originated across India, Nepal, and southern China, this plant comes in slicing, pickling, and seedless types — what is it?
Cucumber: Species of flowering plant with edible fruits.

This acute medical syndrome develops over hours or days and causes disturbed attention, awareness, and sometimes hallucinations — often triggered by illness, substances, or their withdrawal — what is it called?
Delirium: Severe confusion that develops quickly, and often fluctuates in intensity.
A dentist and gambler who fought alongside lawman Wyatt Earp at the O.K. Corral, his reputation claimed dozens of killings though researchers count just one to three — who was this gunfighter?
Doc Holliday: Gambler, gunfighter, and dentist in the American West (1851–1887)
After stints at the CIA, Dell, and Booz Allen Hamilton, this NSA contractor flew to Hong Kong in 2013 and leaked thousands of classified documents exposing global surveillance — who is he?
Edward Snowden: Whistleblower and NSA contractor (born 1983)
One of the four basic animal tissue types, this thin protective cell layer lines blood vessels and body cavities and includes the skin's outer layer — what is it called?
Epithelium: Tissue lining the surfaces of organs in animals.
In this small bird of prey, females can be up to 25% larger than males — one of the biggest size gaps between sexes of any bird — and it hunts garden songbirds across Europe and Asia — which raptor?

Eurasian sparrowhawk: Species of bird. The Eurasian sparrowhawk (Accipiter nisus), also known as the northern sparrowhawk or simply the sparrowhawk, is a small bird of prey in the family Accipitridae.
Marketed under brand names like Allegra, this second-generation antihistamine treats allergy symptoms without crossing the blood-brain barrier the way older drugs do — what medication is it?
Fexofenadine: Antihistamine medication. Fexofenadine is an antihistamine medication used in the treatment of allergy symptoms such as allergic rhinitis and urticaria.
Dead at just 26, this British thinker had already reshaped philosophy, mathematics and economics — and as an undergraduate translated Wittgenstein's 'Tractatus' into English; who was he?
Frank P. Ramsey: British philosopher, mathematician and economist (1903–1930)
With a siphon that can stretch over three feet and a shell just 6 to 8 inches across, this giant Pacific burrowing clam can live up to 179 years — which creature?
Caused by the bacterium Neisseria gonorrhoeae and colloquially called 'the clap,' this sexually transmitted infection can pass from mother to child during birth — what is it?
Gonorrhea: Sexually transmitted infection. Gonorrhea or gonorrhoea, colloquially known as the clap, is a sexually transmitted infection (STI) caused by the bacterium Neisseria gonorrhoeae.
A lentivirus and member of the retrovirus family, it gradually cripples the human immune system — and untreated, leaves roughly 9 to 11 years before the immune collapse called AIDS. What is it?
HIV: Human retrovirus, cause of AIDS. Without treatment, the average survival time after infection with HIV is estimated to be 9 to 11 years, depending on the HIV subtype.

This 19th-century American economist argued in his bestseller 'Progress and Poverty' that a single tax on land values could build a fairer, more productive society — sparking a movement named for him. Who was he?
An American aviator and aerospace engineer who first made his name as a big-budget Hollywood producer, this man grew famous late in life for his reclusive, eccentric ways — who was the magnate?
Howard Hughes: American aviator, aerospace engineer and business magnate (1905–1976)
This family of long-legged wading birds that live in wetlands and forests lent its name — mistakenly — to the scientific name of the western cattle egret in 1757 — what's the bird group called?
Ibis: Long-legged wading birds with down-curved beaks.
A year on the Hijri calendar is how much shorter than a Gregorian one?
Twelve lunar months come to 354 or 355 days against the Gregorian 365, which is why Islamic dates drift backwards through the seasons rather than staying fixed.
This German craftsman's mechanical printing press — with its oil-based ink and adjustable metal type — sparked an information revolution that helped fuel the Renaissance and Reformation — who is he?
Johannes Gutenberg: German inventor and craftsman (c. 1393–1406 – 1468)

A NASA mathematician and human computer, she calculated the orbital mechanics critical to America's first crewed spaceflights and was among the first African-American women to work as a NASA scientist — who was she?
Native to the Mediterranean and used to season food as a bay leaf, this aromatic evergreen prominent in classical Greco-Roman culture can grow up to 20 metres tall — what is its scientific name?
Laurus nobilis: Species of flowering plant in the laurel family Lauraceae.
Nearly always affecting women, this incurable condition causes fat buildup in both legs that's resistant to typical weight loss and often mistaken for other circulatory disorders — what is it?
Lipedema: Condition involving excessive deposition of fat in the legs.
Native to China, Japan, Korea and Nepal and blooming in late summer after heavy rainfall, this plant's alternate names include the hurricane lily and the corpse flower — what is it?
Lycoris radiata: Species of plant. It is originally from China, Japan, Korea and Nepal and spread from there to the United States and elsewhere.

Often making people tall and thin with long fingers and very flexible joints, this connective-tissue disorder carries serious risks to the heart and aorta — caused by a mutation in the FBN1 fibrillin gene — which condition?
Marfan syndrome: Genetic disorder involving connective tissue.

Fever, a fierce headache, neck stiffness, and a telltale rash that doesn't fade when a glass is rolled over it can signal this inflammation of the membranes around the brain and spinal cord — what is it?

Meningitis: Inflammation of membranes around the brain. Meningitis (pl. meningitides) is acute or chronic inflammation of the protective membranes covering the brain and spinal cord, collectively called the meninges.

Soviet pilots called it the "Balalaika" because its planform looked like the stringed instrument, while Poles dubbed it "Ołówek" — the pencil — for its slender fuselage; which most-produced supersonic jet in history earned all those nicknames?
Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-21: 1956 Soviet fighter aircraft family.
Nicknamed noni, this pungent-smelling fruit tree in the coffee family was spread across the Pacific by Polynesian sailors and is now used mainly in traditional medicine and juices — which plant?
Morinda citrifolia: Species of plant. It is commonly known as noni or Indian mulberry, among many other names.
Sold under the brand name Deca-Durabolin, this anabolic steroid is prescribed for conditions like anemia and osteoporosis despite masculinizing side effects — which compound?
Nandrolone: Androgenic Anabolic steroid. Nandrolone, also known as 19-nortestosterone, is an endogenous androgen.
Discovered in 1846 by Ascanio Sobrero, this oily explosive liquid became the key ingredient in dynamite — what is it?
Causing white or yellow discoloration, thickening, and lifting of the nail — and far more often striking toenails than fingernails — what is this fungal infection also called tinea unguium?
Named by Reginald Innes Pocock in 1917 to cover big cats of genus Panthera, this cat subfamily later grew to include the clouded leopards too — which subfamily?
Pantherinae: Subfamily of felids. The Pantherinae genetically diverged from a common ancestor between 9.32 to 4.47 million years ago and 10.67 to 3.76 million years ago.
A hybrid cross of watermint and spearmint, this herb is one of the oldest used in cooking and medicine and a key plant source of menthol — what is it?
Peppermint: Hybrid flowering plant in the family Lamiaceae.
This healthcare profession uses patient education and hands-on interventions to prevent, treat, and restore mobility, with specialties from sports medicine to pediatrics — which field?
Physical therapy: Profession that helps a disabled person function in everyday life.
This large, structurally diverse family of plant compounds includes flavonoids and tannic acid, some of which were historically used as dyes and for tanning garments — what are they called?
Also called cherry laurel, this evergreen shrub native to the Black Sea region was once woven into wreaths for its resemblance to true bay laurel, though the two aren't closely related — which plant?
Prunus laurocerasus: Species of plant. It is not to be confused with its American relative Prunus caroliniana, which is also called cherry laurel.

Historically nicknamed 'hydrophobia' because sufferers panic at the offer of a drink, this viral disease causes severe brain inflammation and is virtually always fatal once symptoms appear. What is it?
Rabies: Deadly viral disease, transmitted through animals.
Nicknamed golden root or Arctic root, this Crassulaceae plant is popular in herbal supplements even though the FDA has warned sellers against overselling its health benefits — which plant?
Rhodiola rosea: Species of flowering plant in the stonecrop family.
A synthetic element named for a famous physicist, it's the first of the super-heavy transactinides and behaves chemically as the heavier cousin of hafnium in group 4 — which element?
Rutherfordium: Chemical element with atomic number 104 (Rf)
Exceeding 30 centimeters in length, this centipede from South America is the largest of its kind, preying on animals as large as small mammals and reptiles — which species?

Scolopendra gigantea: Species of Chilopoda (centipede). Scolopendra gigantea, also known as the Peruvian giant yellow-leg centipede or Amazonian giant centipede, is a centipede in the genus Scolopendra.
Made up of the collarbone, the scapula, and the upper-arm bone meeting in a ball-and-socket joint, which body part lets the arm swing in a full circle?
Shoulder: Part of the body. The articulations between the bones of the shoulder make up the shoulder joints.
This frozen dessert blends ice with fruit juice or purée — and sometimes wine, liqueur, or honey — for a refreshing icy treat. What is it called?
Sorbet: Frozen dessert. Sorbet is a frozen dessert made using ice combined with fruit juice, fruit purée, or other ingredients, such as wine, liqueur, or honey.

Striking about one in a million people, this rare neurological disorder brings progressive muscular rigidity and spasms that twist the trunk into postural deformities — first described in 1956, what is it?
Stiff-person syndrome: Neurological disorder. The stiffness primarily affects the truncal muscles and is characterised by spasms, resulting in postural deformities.

This red-orange, sublimable heterocyclic solid is a stable aminoxyl radical used as a spin probe in electron spin resonance spectroscopy and as a mediator in controlled radical polymerization — what's this compound commonly called?
This group of inherited blood disorders reduces hemoglobin production and is classified as alpha or beta depending on which globin gene is deficient. What condition is it?
Thalassemia: Family of inherited blood disorders. Symptoms depend on the type of thalassemia and can vary from none to severe, including death.

A nightshade cousin of tobacco and chili peppers, its edible berry was carried from western South America to Eurasia by the Spanish during the Columbian exchange — which fruit, eaten as a vegetable, is it?
Tomato: Edible berry. The tomato (US:, UK:; Solanum lycopersicum) is a plant whose fruit is an edible berry that is eaten as a vegetable.
A member of the ginger family native to the Indian subcontinent, its boiled and dried rhizomes are ground into a deep orange-yellow powder used to color and flavor curries — what is it?
This hairy biennial plant can top two meters, packing small yellow flowers onto a tall spike that sprouts from a low leaf rosette in disturbed, sunlit soil — which weedy species?
Verbascum thapsus: Species of plant. It is a hairy biennial plant that can grow to 2 m tall or more.

Distinguished by its wide, square-lipped mouth built for grazing, this is the largest and most social species in its family; its northern subspecies lost its last known male, Sudan, in 2018 — which animal?
White rhinoceros: Species of large land mammal.
Tracing its formal origins to Aristotle and later shaped by Carl Linnaeus, this branch of biology studies the structure, classification and behavior of animals — which field?
The symbol for hassium is Hs. Hassium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Hs and atomic number 108.
The symbol for actinium is Ac. Actinium is a chemical element; it has symbol Ac and atomic number 89.

In what year was Ian Somerhalder born?
Ian Somerhalder: Ian Joseph Somerhalder ( SUM-ər-hawl-dər; born December 8, 1978) is a retired American actor.
In what year was Emma Thompson born?
Emma Thompson: Dame Emma Thompson (born 15 April 1959) is a British actress and screenwriter.
In what year was David Schwimmer born?
David Schwimmer: David Lawrence Schwimmer (born November 2, 1966) is an American actor, director, comedian and producer.
In what year was Anya Taylor-Joy born?
Anya Taylor-Joy: Anya-Josephine Marie Taylor-Joy (born 16 April 1996) is an actress.
In what year was Dakota Johnson born?
